notes: Letter b [b] 'not found in native words' (p. 123): loans (Bennis 'Friday' from Chamorro, bileet 'blade' from English). Distinct from bw (p. 27).
Letter d [d] 'not found in native words except in Tanapag' (p. 148): in the southern dialects, loans from Chamorro, Japanese, English and Spanish (dakkun, daikon, dais, danamita).

Letter g, 'used in writing the Tanapag (Enne) dialect and in borrowed words' (p. 187): in the southern dialects, loans (gakko 'school', ganna 'win'); Tanapag g corresponds to southern gh (gareeta, see ghareeta). The value on p. 27 is printed in a substitute font ([Ω], compared with English go).
Letter z [dz] 'not found in native words' (p. 489): loans from English and Japanese (zaam 'jam', zoori 'slippers').

Letter n [n]: the LN dialect 'has both l and n consonant sounds, the EL dialect has only l' (p. xxi), and the Tanapag dialect has n; otherwise in loans. Ellis (2012: 160-161) counts 26 headwords in n, most of them loans or LN and Tanapag words.
Single k is 'not found singly in native words' (p. 229); native words have kk. Unaspirated (p. 27).
